request.spec:
A fourth role, restricted, can be assigned. A restricted user sees on the people list only the
people of the crews they lead or belong to (by a person with the user's name) and that person
themselves: no other row is on the screen. Every other figure (the totals row, the header, the
summary, the periods, the pools) is still over everyone on the sheet.

agent.result_text:
I added a fourth role, `restricted`, and all 4 acceptance tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

**What changed:**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V93__role_restricted.sql`, rebuilds `sheet_role` so its check also allows `restricted` (the same way the viewer migration did).
- **Server:** `Role.RESTRICTED` is added, and `ValidateRole` now accepts it. Any other role, such as `x`, is still refused and writes nothing to the audit file. Assigning a role still writes the existing `ROLE_SET` audit record.
- **Front end:**
  - The roles form (`Roles.tsx`) now offers `restricted`.
  - In `People.tsx`, a restricted user's list shows only their own person and the people of the crews they lead or belong to, both the lead and the members. Their own person is the one whose name or alias matches the user's name, ignoring case and surrounding spaces, the same rule the header's "my" figures use.
  - A restricted user with no person of their own on the sheet sees no rows.
  - The totals row, header, summary, periods and pools are worked out on the screen from the full people list, so they still cover everyone on the sheet.

**Things to know:**
- **The filter is only on the screen.** The server still sends every person to the browser, because those other figures need the full list. A restricted user who looks at the network traffic can see everyone. Hiding that on the server would mean computing those figures on the server, which is a much bigger change.
- **The list starts empty.** It shows no rows until the user's role has loaded, so a restricted user never briefly sees everyone. If the role can't be loaded at all, the list stays empty rather than showing everyone.
- **Restricted users can't take the guarded actions** (open, settle, void, close and so on) under the default permissions, which allow only clerks and stewards. The request didn't say what a restricted user may change, so I didn't touch permissions. A `perm-<action>` setting that names `restricted` would allow it.
